messages:
maya: @alex customer reports intermittent truncated SSE when connecting from behind a corporate proxy. connection closes ~25-35s. first seen ~2026-03-15T14:22Z. request-id: rwd-0a1b2c3d, trace: t-9f8e7d. they tried a basic curl and got EOF. need minimal curl repro and what exact headers we should ask for. :mag:

alex: can you ask for the full request-id (root) and the raw response headers? also ask them to run curl with verbosity and no buffering so we see the wire: `curl -v --no-buffer --http1.1 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Connection: keep-alive" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 'https://api.redwood.inference/v1/streams?model=gpt-redwood'`  -- that usually exposes proxy behavior. remind them to keep the token redacted in the bundle. :thumbsup:

maya: pasted the root request-id above (rwd-0a1b2c3d). customer says proxy mutates chunked frames. posting a checklist we want them to run and upload:

1) exact curl command they used
2) output of `curl -v --no-buffer --http1.1 --trace-ascii curl-trace.txt -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Connection: keep-alive" -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" 'https://api.redwood.inference/v1/streams?model=gpt-redwood'`
3) full response headers (raw)
4) proxy logs for the time window (include upstream/downstream bytes and any `Connection:` rewrites)
5) if they're using our HMAC, include the X-Redwood-Signature header value (do NOT include secrets)

Also adding a minimal example they can copy/paste:

```
TOKEN=<REDACTED>
curl -v --no-buffer --http1.1 \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  'https://api.redwood.inference/v1/streams?model=gpt-redwood'
```

alex: if they're using HMAC auth instead of bearer, ask for both the `X-Redwood-Signature` and `X-Redwood-Timestamp` headers we log. also ask them to try forcing HTTP/1.1 (`--http1.1`) because some proxies downgrade to HTTP/2 and that can change streaming behavior. if they can reproduce locally (no proxy) that's a good signal it's the proxy.

john: adding a short HMAC curl snippet for teams that sign requests server-side (they can redact secrets):

```
TIMESTAMP=$(date +%s)
SIGN=$(printf "%s\n%s" "$TIMESTAMP" "/v1/streams" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$SECRET" -binary | base64)
curl -v -N --http1.1 \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Timestamp: $TIMESTAMP" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Signature: $SIGN" \
  'https://api.redwood.inference/v1/streams?model=gpt-redwood'
```

logs-bot: uploaded diag bundle for this session: rwd-bundle-2068451234.tar.gz -> https://internal.redwood/suppruns/rwd-bundle-2068451234 (contains proxy headers, tcpdump snippet, and service trace for rwd-0a1b2c3d).

maya: customer attached their curl trace. key lines:
`* Connected to api.redwood.inference (52.3.2.1) port 443 (#0)`
`> GET /v1/streams?model=gpt-redwood HTTP/1.1`
`> Host: api.redwood.inference`
`> Accept: text/event-stream`
`> Connection: keep-alive`
`< HTTP/1.1 200 OK`
`< content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`
`< transfer-encoding: chunked`
`...data chunks...`
`* Received EOF`
`* Closing connection 0`

That EOF matches the proxy logs that show a FIN from the proxy at the same timestamp.

sam: can we ask them to run a long-lived simple httpbin stream (or `sse` demo) through the same proxy to determine whether the proxy cuts all long-lived connections or only our endpoint? also ask them to disable any content-length rewrite rules if possible. :thinking_face:

alex: next steps for us:
- confirm whether the proxy is idle-time killing or seeing a malformed chunk boundary (logs suggest the proxy injected `Connection: close`).
- if the proxy is killing, recommend keepalive pings or adjust proxy timeout. we can also offer `heartbeat` SSE comment pings from our side as a temporary mitigation (eng-runtime FYI).

maya: I've asked the customer to run the checklist and attach the `curl-trace.txt` and proxy logs. once we have those I can reproduce locally behind a similar proxy config. if they can't share proxy internals, ask for a sanitized snippet with timestamps. :raised_hands:

john: if we can reproduce, I'll open an eng-runtime issue and include the trace, request-id rwd-0a1b2c3d, and the diag bundle link. otherwise escalate to networking for packet-level analysis.

maya: thanks everyone — I'll follow up once customer uploads the traces. closing the loop here for now. :wave:
